headline: Canada’s Carney Says US Has Lowered Its Demands in Trade Talks
content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said the US is “asking less” and “offering more” in trade negotiations, as the neighboring nations once again work on a potential deal after a previous round of talks collapsed. “Some of our red lines have clearly shifted, around language, around culture, around sovereignty, our ability to have trade deals. In other words, those are now off the table. That’s very welcome,” Carney told reporters during a trip to Antigua and Barbuda, where’s he attending a meeting of Commonwealth leaders. In August, the US and Canada were close to an agreement to reduce tariffs and other trade barriers, but it fell apart, leading each side to put 50% duties on a list of products from the other.At the time, Carney said the US had sought to curtail Canadian protections around the French language and culture, and to restrain its ability to sign trade deals with other partners. US officials accused Carney of blowing up the talks for domestic political reasons, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick saying he didn’t care about Canadian language rules. English and French are Canada’s two official languages. “There are other important issues on which we still need to make progress,” Carney added. “If I were to paraphrase it, they’re asking less and they’re offering more — but we’re not quite there.”The feud between the two countries erupted nearly two years ago after President Donald Trump was reelected, announced plans for tariffs and said he’d like to make Canada a 51st state. But both sides have recently sounded more positive on the prospect of a detente that would ease trade frictions.Earlier on Tuesday, Trump said the US will make a “great deal” with Canada “soon.” He has hinted at elements of a possible deal, stating the US would have tariff-free access to fertilizers and that Canada would build and pay for a southbound oil pipeline. Canada has not put any export taxes or duties on potash, a key fertilizer input, which it supplies in large quantities to the US. The pipeline project that Trump was referring to already has commercial backers, and the Canadian firm involved, South Bow Corp., is targeting a final investment decision next year. Carney didn’t share specific details about negotiations related to the auto sector, which proved a critical stumbling block last time. Despite decades of deep cross-border supply-chain integration, Trump has said he doesn’t want the US to import Canadian vehicles. ©2026 Bloomberg L.P.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: UP court dismisses revision plea against Kangana Ranaut in 'gutter generation' remark case
content: Agra, Uttar Pradesh: A district court has dismissed a revision petition filed against the rejection of a complaint against actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut over her alleged "gutter generation" remark, a lawyer who filed the case said on Tuesday. .Advocate Ramshankar Sharma, who had filed the complaint against Ranaut, said District Judge Sanjay Kumar Malik dismissed the revision petition. .Earlier, MP-MLA court judge Anuj Kumar on Monday dismissed the complaint, following which Sharma approached the district judge with a revision petition challenging the order. .Opposition's 'low-level acts' reinforce need for PM Modi's leadership: Kangana Ranaut.Sharma said he would now approach the Allahabad High Court in the matter. .Ranaut, who represents Himachal Pradesh's Mandi in the Lok Sabha, had allegedly used the term "gutter generation" while referring to a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. .Following the remark, a complaint was filed against her in the MP-MLA court in Agra.

headline: IIT Mandi in Himachal Pradesh: Courses, research facilities, placements and what students should know
content: The Indian Institute of Technology Mandi (IIT Mandi) is a public technical university in the Kamand Valley of Himachal Pradesh . It was established in 2009 as one of the second-generation IITs and has the motto ‘Scaling the heights!’. The institute has nine schools and more than six research centres. It offers B.Tech, M.Tech, MBA, MA, M.Sc and PhD programmes. In NIRF 2025 it ranked 26th in engineering, 58th overall and 10th in innovation. IIT Mandi history and establishment The foundation stone was laid in February 2009. The first batch of 97 students was admitted in July 2009, with classes starting in July at IIT Roorkee, the mentoring IIT. Prof. Timothy A. Gonsalves joined as Founding Director in January 2010. A transit campus was set up at Vallabh Government College, Mandi, whose buildings the Himachal Pradesh Government handed over in November 2009, and classes began in Mandi in August 2010. Construction in Kamand started in April 2012, and the first batch moved to the Kamand campus in September 2012. IIT Mandi became the first of the newer IITs to shift all B.Tech students to its permanent campus, in April 2015. The campus covers about 538 acres near the Uhl River, around 14 km from Mandi town. It is divided into a North and a South campus connected by a narrow neck. The institute has also run community programmes, including Enabling Women of Kamand (EWOK), launched in 2016. IIT Mandi academics and admissions B.Tech branches include Computer Science, Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, Electrical, Mechanical, Civil and Infrastructure, Engineering Physics and Mathematics and Computing. Admission to B.Tech is through JEE Advanced and JoSAA counselling. M.Tech uses GATE, M.Sc uses IIT-JAM and MBA uses CAT. First-semester B.Tech fees are about ₹1.18 lakh. Its design practicum, a first-semester course aimed at building research habits, is often singled out by students. IIT Mandi JEE Advanced cut-offs CSE is the most competitive branch and its closing rank has been remarkably stable. The General-category closing rank in the final round was about 2,909 in 2023, 3,118 in 2024 and 3,123 in 2025. In 2025 Round 1, CSE ran from an opening rank of 2,096 to a closing rank of 3,087. Electrical Engineering closed at about 6,474 and Civil Engineering at about 12,346 in that round. In the 2026 counselling, CSE closed at 3,609 in Round 1 and 3,701 by Round 4. Reserved-category and female-only seats close at separate ranks, and JoSAA remains the authoritative source. IIT Mandi placements In 2025, 222 B.Tech students sat for placements and 211 were placed, a rate of 95.04%, with a median package of ₹17 lakh. A total of 266 companies took part, and CSE reported a 100% placement rate with an average package of about ₹29.3 lakh. One reports a B.Tech highest package of ₹65 lakh and an overall average of ₹21.64 lakh, though it uses a different cohort count, so I would treat the figures as indicative. MBA outcomes were a median of ₹12 lakh, an average of ₹16 lakh and a highest of ₹39 lakh. Recruiters include Accenture, Adobe, Cisco, Cognizant and Airtel. Earlier B.Tech medians were higher, at ₹22 lakh in 2022–23, so the 2025 figure suggests some softening. IIT Mandi student and alumni voices One student summed up the institute as "A beautiful IIT with Himalayan views, good placements, and brilliant minds." Another titled a review "IIT Mandi: The heart of nature." A reviewer said hostel life is better than at other IITs, and the hostels have elevators. Another reviewer noted that placements for computer science students were almost 100%. Students also report strong support for sport, with several active clubs. The alumni voice is documented in the institute's tenth Foundation Day release. A member of the first B.Tech batch (2009–13) said he and his batchmates were "honoured and privileged" to be part of the institute. Prof. Gonsalves described IIT Mandi at the same event as "a jewel in the Himalayan crown of India." Alumni named by the institute include Athar Aamir Khan, who secured All India Rank 2 in the UPSC civil services examination of 2015, and Pradeep Seervi, who obtained All India Rank 1 in GATE 2015. Others are Shubham Ajmera, the first IIT Mandi student placed at Google, Dhirendra Kumar Singh, the institute's first student entrepreneur, and Dr. Mohit Kumar Malhotra, a scientist in the Ministry of Defence. Srimanta Mandal is listed as an associate professor. IIT Mandi combines a scenic residential campus, steady CSE cut-offs and consistently high placement rates. Median packages have eased from earlier peaks, and value for money rates lower than other criteria. Applicants should compare branch-wise results and the latest JoSAA data before deciding.

headline: Public Should Celebrate Festivals in an Environmentally Responsible Manner: Tamil Nadu Minister for Environment and Climate Change Dr. V. K. Rajeev
content: The Press Information Bureau , Chennai, in collaboration with the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB), organised a Media Workshop on “Promoting Environment-Friendly Lifestyles” on 03 November 2026 in Chennai. The workshop was inaugurated by Dr. V. K. Rajeev, Minister for Environment and Climate Change, Government of Tamil Nadu. The programme focused on sustainable lifestyles, circular economy, environmental protection and eco-friendly celebrations, with participation from government officials, environmental experts and media representatives. Addressing the gathering, the Minister urged the public to celebrate festivals without causing harm to the environment. Emphasising the need to avoid harmful chemicals in the manufacture of firecrackers during Deepavali, he encouraged the use of green crackers manufactured in accordance with the guidelines of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research - National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI). He also advised the public to purchase only crackers bearing the green cracker logo and verify their authenticity through the QR code. Pointing out that air and noise pollution caused by firecrackers adversely affect children and people with respiratory ailments, the Minister urged the public to adhere to the time restrictions prescribed by the Government. He announced that solar lights would be provided to villages located near bird sanctuaries that have voluntarily refrained from bursting firecrackers for several years. He also stated that large-scale plantation of trees suitable for birds would be undertaken in these villages. The Minister stressed the need to reduce plastic usage and adopt biodegradable alternatives. Conveying the message, “Celebrate more, pollute less”, he urged the public to celebrate Deepavali in an environment-friendly manner. Shri. Anurag Mishra, Chairman, Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, in his special address, highlighted the importance of environmental protection, sustainable use of natural resources, responsible consumption and waste reduction. He emphasised that public participation and media-led awareness initiatives were essential to creating a clean and green environment. Delivering the introductory address, Shri. J. Kamaraj, Additional Director General, Press Information Bureau, Chennai, highlighted the important role of the media in taking environmental awareness to the public. He noted that journalists play a vital role in communicating scientific and technological information in a simple and accessible manner and in encouraging public participation in environmental protection.

headline: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) and Government of Bihar Sign MoU for Scientific Desilting of Water Bodies and Utilisation of Silt in National Highway Projects
content: In a significant step towards integrating water-body restoration with infrastructure development, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and the Government of Bihar today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for scientific desilting of identified rivers and other water bodies and utilisation of suitable excavated silt in National Highway construction projects in Bihar. The MoU was signed in New Delhi in the presence of Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari and Bihar Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary. Envisioned as ‘Nadi Sanjivani’, the initiative seeks to restore the water-carrying capacity of rivers and water bodies, strengthen flood management, conserve agricultural land and provide a sustainable source of construction material for National Highway projects. It presents an integrated approach to addressing water-management challenges while supporting infrastructure expansion. Addressing the gathering, Shri Nitin Gadkari highlighted that accumulated silt has significantly affected the carrying capacity of rivers, contributing to floods, damage to agricultural land and loss of property. Bihar faces recurring challenges of flooding and water scarcity, particularly due to rivers originating in Nepal that carry substantial quantities of water and sediment into the State. He emphasised that scientific desilting would help improve water flow and drainage, restore water bodies and make suitable excavated material available for highway construction. The Union Minister stated that the initiative would create a mutually beneficial framework in which river restoration supports infrastructure development, while utilisation of excavated silt reduces dependence on fresh earth material and agricultural soil. This would help conserve productive agricultural land, reduce construction costs and facilitate faster completion of highway projects. He further emphasised that implementation would be undertaken in coordination with the Bihar Government with appropriate technical assessments and safeguards. Expressing confidence in the initiative, Shri Gadkari said that the model could be extended to other States facing similar challenges, promoting sustainable infrastructure development and improved water management. Shri Samrat Choudhary, Chief Minister of Bihar, highlighted the State’s longstanding vulnerability to recurring floods, which cause substantial losses to farmers, agricultural land, livelihoods and infrastructure. He underscored the need for scientific management of rivers and water bodies to address the adverse impact of accumulated silt on their water-carrying capacity. The Chief Minister informed that the Bihar Water Sources Restoration and Silt Management Policy, 2026, has been formulated to provide a structured framework for restoration of water bodies and management of accumulated silt. The policy also facilitates removal of sand and silt deposited on agricultural land following floods, providing relief to affected farmers.

headline: Thousands displaced as homes are bulldozed in India’s Assam state
content: Thousands displaced as homes are bulldozed in India’s Assam state Hundreds of homes have been bulldozed in the Dhubri district of Assam state in northeastern India as part of a government campaign to evict families it says do not legally live there. Local media says most of the 4,000 people displaced were Bengali-speaking Muslims.

headline: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Inaugurated Microbiology Laboratory, Launched Churpi Traceability Initiative and Fodder Plus FPO Products in Sikkim
content: Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Alias Lalan Singh), Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, participated in a programme organised by the Sikkim Milk Union (SMU) at Gangtok, Sikkim, on 3 November 2026. The programme focused on strengthening dairy infrastructure, expanding cooperative networks and promoting value addition in the dairy sector. The Hon’ble Union Minister inaugurated the Microbiology Laboratory of the Sikkim Milk Union under the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD). The facility was aimed at strengthening microbiological testing and quality assessment, thereby contributing to improved quality assurance and food safety in the dairy sector. He also inspected the exhibition stalls showcasing dairy products and other initiatives of the Sikkim Milk Union. The programme commenced with a welcome address by the Chairman of the Sikkim Milk Union, followed by the felicitation of the Hon’ble Union Minister and other dignitaries. The Microbiology Laboratory at Karfectar was also virtually inaugurated. The Churpi Traceability initiative was inaugurated to strengthen traceability and promote the identity and marketability of the traditional dairy product. The Hon’ble Union Minister also witnessed the launch of Fodder Plus products developed by Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), highlighting the importance of fodder availability, farmer collectives and diversified income opportunities in the livestock sector. Registration certificates were distributed to five newly established Dairy Cooperative Societies (DCSs), marking another step towards strengthening the cooperative dairy network in Sikkim and expanding the reach of organised dairy institutions at the grassroots level. Sikkim recorded 79% growth in milk production over the last decade Addressing the gathering, the Hon’ble Union Minister congratulated the Government of Sikkim and stakeholders on the significant progress made in the dairy sector. He highlighted that milk production had increased by 79%, from 1.37 lakh litres to 2.45 lakh litres per day, while the number of dairy cooperative societies had grown by 88%, from 389 in 2014–15 to 733 in 2025–26. Daily milk supply to consumers had also doubled from 28,000 litres to 56,000 litres.

headline: From Helsinki to Bologna: Rethinking Finnish History Through Una Europa Doctoral Programme
content: Doctoral researcher Iisa Aaltonen explores the public memory culture of Finland’s Independence Day and is completing her dissertation at two universities within Una Europa’s Cultural Heritage doctoral programme. The programme has taken her on an exchange to Bologna and offered new perspectives on cultural heritage, academic practices and the analysis of Finnish history. Iisa Aaltonen is a historian, with a Master of Arts degree from the University of Helsinki, and she has also completed a master’s degree in cultural policy at the University of Jyväskylä. Aaltonen found her way to Una Europa’s international doctoral programme through a recommendation from her supervisor. What particularly interested her in the programme were its diverse perspectives on cultural heritage, the opportunity for international experiences and networks, and a broader view of the academic world. Studying in the international Una Europa alliance has provided both the support of an academic community extending beyond Finland’s borders and new perspectives on her research. Aaltonen is completing her dissertation simultaneously at two universities, and one of her supervisors is from the University of Bologna. She has spent the past 12 months on exchange at the University of Bologna. The exchange period has been an eye-opening experience. In Bologna, she has taken part in a doctoral researchers’ seminar whose working methods differ from those of seminars at the University of Helsinki. Whereas in Finland the focus is often on discussing doctoral researchers’ own texts, in Bologna the seminars have consisted more of lectures by visiting speakers. Both approaches have offered useful methodological perspectives and literature recommendations. The international environment has also helped Aaltonen examine her own research topic in a new way.

headline: DA hike: Tamil Nadu, MP, Himachal, Rajasthan, Kerala — Full list of states with dearness allowance hikes ahead of Diwali
content: The Union Cabinet has hiked dearness allowance by 3% for central government employees and pensioners, raising the component from 60% to 63% of basic pay, effective from 1 July, as per the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) recommendation.Under the 7th CPC recommendations, DA is revised twice a year, using data from the All-India Consumer Price Index (AICPI). This “Diwali gift” is the second DA increase this year, after the Centre hiked the component by 2% in April from 58% to 60%, effective from 1 January.DA is a percentage of employees' basic pay that aims to mitigate the impact of the rising cost of living and inflation. Usually, announcements from the Centre come in March and October, with rollouts in January and July. Over 1 crore beneficiaries — about 50 lakh central government employees and nearly 65 lakh pensioners, including defence and railway personnel and retirees gain from DA and dearness relief (DR) hikes.States hike DA ahead of Diwali 2026 — Full listBesides the Finance Ministry's announcement on 28 October, state governments also hiked DA for employees and pensioners ahead of Diwali. This includes a 5% hike by the Himachal Pradesh government, 3% DA hikes each by the Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan governments, and 2% increases by the Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Keralam governments.Tamil Nadu on 31 October announced a 3% DA hike, from the existing 60% rate to 63% ahead of the “Diwali festival of joy”, for state government employees, teachers and pensioners. Benefiting around 16 lakh state government employees, teachers, pensioners, and family pensioners, the increase will be effective from 1 July 2026 and will cost the state exchequer ₹1,858 crore annually, it said. This is the second DA increase this year — the state also hiked DA by 2% to 60% of basic pay, effective from 1 January at additional annual expenditure of ₹1,230 crore.Rajasthan on 30 October approved a 3% increase in DA and DR for state employees and pensioners to 63% of basic pay. Over 7 lakh government employees and over 5 lakh pensioners will benefit from the revision, effective from 1 July 2026, “as a Diwali gift,” at an additional financial burden of ₹820 crore on the state exchequer. The increase will be paid in the November and December salaries, respectively, while arrears for the four-month period from July to October will be deposited in their General Provident Fund (GPF) accounts.Also on 30 October, Madhya Pradesh announced a 2% DA hike for state government employees, including officers and pensioners, ahead of Diwali, with effect from 1 January. CM Mohan Yadav said arrears for nine months, from January to September, will be paid in three equal monthly instalments. From October, the increased DA will be paid in cash with salaries (October's DA payable in November salary). Meanwhile, DR will be effective from July.The Chhattisgarh government on 29 October hiked DA by 2%, taking it to 60% of basic pay from the existing 58%, with effect from 1 November, at an additional financial burden of around ₹36 crore per month and ₹432 crore annually on the state exchequer. “The state government is sensitive to the interests of its employees and pensioners. This decision taken ahead of Diwali will provide financial relief and enhance festive cheer among their families. The decision will benefit around 3.85 lakh state government employees and 1.5 lakh pensioners,” CM Vishnu Deo Sai said.Earlier in the month, Himachal Pradesh increased DA by 5%, from 45% to 50%, for eligible state government employees covered by the Himachal Pradesh Civil Services (Revised Pay) Rules, 2022, All India Services officers and state government employees covered by UGC pay scales. The additional DA will be paid in cash with the October 2026 salary, payable in November 2026.Kerala hiked DA and DR by 2% from 35% to 37%, to be paid with the October 2026 salary, disbursed in November, for state government employees, teachers, full-time contingent employees and local government staff, state service pensioners, family pensioners, and eligible ex-gratia pensioners and their families. This was the second increase following a 10% hike from 25% to 35% in February 2026. The state said it will provide additional relief to eligible employees and pensioners amid rising inflation and turbulent geopolitical times. It added that separate arrears orders will clarify the payment of pending dues.Notably, after the Centre's April announcement, the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) revised the DA and DR for employees for May, June and July 2026. Later, the Indian Railways also announced a 2% hike in DA and DR for staff and pensioners. Further, several states also followed the DA and DR hike announcements, including Telangana, Sikkim, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Maharashtra, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.

headline: Sugs Lloyd Reports 73 Percent Revenue Growth and 69 Percent Rise in PAT in H1 FY27
content: VMPLNoida (Uttar Pradesh) [India], November 2: Sugs Lloyd Limited (BSE SME: 544501), an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) company engaged in Power Transmission and Distribution (T & D), solar and smart-grid solutions across India, has announced its standalone financial results for the half-year ended September 30, 2026.Q2 FY27 revenue more than doubles year-on-year to ₹134.9 crore; company secures ₹395 crore in new orders during the quarter, with an outstanding order book of ₹1,068 croreThe company recorded its highest-ever half-yearly revenue of ₹213.31 crore and profit after tax (PAT) of ₹20.01 crore, representing year-on-year growth of 73% and 69%, respectively. The performance was supported by accelerated execution of its order book, particularly the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) smart-grid project, during the second quarter.Key Financial Highlights: H1 FY27- Revenue from Operations: ₹213.31 crore in H1 FY27, compared with ₹123.03 crore in H1 FY26, registering growth of 73%.- EBITDA: ₹31.00 crore, compared with ₹18.88 crore in H1 FY26, representing an increase of 64%.- EBITDA Margin: 14.54% in H1 FY27, compared with 15.34% in H1 FY26, reflecting a decline of 81 basis points.- Profit After Tax: ₹20.01 crore, compared with ₹11.82 crore in H1 FY26, registering growth of 69%.- PAT Margin: 9.38%, compared with 9.61% in the corresponding period of the previous financial year, a decline of 23 basis points.- Earnings Per Share (Basic and Diluted): ₹8.62, compared with ₹6.86 in H1 FY26, representing growth of 26%.EPS is not annualised and is calculated on the weighted average number of shares. IPO shares were allotted in September 2025, so H1 FY26 EPS is based on a lower share count. EBITDA excludes other income.Quarterly Performance: Q2 FY27- Revenue from Operations: ₹134.91 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹63.62 crore in Q2 FY26, registering year-on-year growth of 112%. Revenue increased 72% quarter-on-quarter from ₹78.40 crore in Q1 FY27.- EBITDA: ₹19.01 crore, compared with ₹9.97 crore in Q2 FY26, representing year-on-year growth of 91%. EBITDA increased 59% quarter-on-quarter from ₹11.99 crore in Q1 FY27.- EBITDA Margin: 14.09% in Q2 FY27, compared with 15.68% in Q2 FY26, reflecting a decline of 159 basis points. The margin stood at 15.30% in Q1 FY27, indicating a quarter-on-quarter decline of 121 basis points.- PAT Margin: 9.27% in Q2 FY27, compared with 9.48% in Q2 FY26, a decline of 21 basis points. The margin was 9.57% in Q1 FY27, reflecting a quarter-on-quarter decline of 30 basis points.The company reports its financial results half-yearly. Q2 figures are derived by subtracting the Q1 figures published on July 30, 2026, from the H1 figures. Q2 FY26 figures are similarly derived by subtracting Q1 FY26 from H1 FY26.The company reported revenue growth of 73% year-on-year in H1 FY27, while second-quarter revenue increased 112% to ₹134.9 crore. The quarterly performance reflected both billing generated during Q2 and billing carried forward from June, as indicated during the company's Q1 earnings call.Growth was primarily driven by the Power T & D and Smart Grid vertical, which contributed 80% of H1 revenue, compared with 46% in FY26. Solar EPC accounted for the remaining 20%.EBITDA margin for H1 FY27 stood at 14.54%, compared with 15.34% in H1 FY26. Finance costs increased 51% to ₹5.89 crore, primarily due to higher working-capital borrowings.Balance Sheet and Cash FlowThe company's standalone balance sheet reflected the following financial position:- Net Worth: ₹157.22 crore as of September 30, 2026, compared with ₹137.21 crore as of March 31, 2026.- Total Borrowings: ₹163.07 crore as of September 30, 2026, compared with ₹68.94 crore as of March 31, 2026.- Debt-to-Equity Ratio: 1.04x, compared with 0.50x as of March 31, 2026.- Trade Receivables: ₹150 crore, compared with ₹139 crore.- Inventories: ₹12 crore, compared with ₹11 crore.- Trade Payables: ₹75 crore, compared with ₹61 crore.- Capital Work-in-Progress: ₹37.05 crore as of September 30, 2026, compared with no reported amount as of March 31, 2026.- Cash Flow from Operations: ₹(12.31) crore in H1 FY27, compared with ₹(37.39) crore for the full year FY26.Working capital increased with the scale-up of the Patna project, funded largely through working-capital facilities. Capital work-in-progress of ₹37.05 crore primarily relates to assets under development for the NBPDCL rooftop solar project under the CAPEX-plus-RESCO model.Operational Highlights- Outstanding Order Book: ₹1,068 crore as of September 30, 2026.- Highest-Ever Half-Yearly Revenue: H1 FY27 revenue of ₹213.31 crore represents 71% of full-year FY26 revenue of ₹300.73 crore.- New Order Wins: Seven orders secured during Q2 FY27, valued at ₹466.43 crore including GST and ₹395.28 crore excluding GST.- Quarterly Order Inflow: ₹395 crore excluding GST, equivalent to 2.9 times Q2 revenue.- Subsidiary Acquisition: On August 21, 2026, the company acquired the shareholding of Sugs Renewables Private Limited, which is now a wholly owned subsidiary.- Operational Presence: The company's operational network spans 11 states: Delhi, Bihar, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Meghalaya and Chhattisgarh.- Qualified Bid Pipeline: ₹2,500 crore, with ₹1,207 crore under evaluation as of September 30, 2026. Management has indicated an expected strike rate of 15-20% on qualified bids.- Industry Recognition: The company was recognised as Best Integrated T & D and Solar EPC Company of the Year at the EPS Energy Awards 2026.Business Outlook and Growth GuidanceSugs Lloyd Limited continues to operate in a sector supported by government-led infrastructure development and power distribution reforms. The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) involves an investment commitment of approximately ₹3.04 lakh crore towards smart metering and grid strengthening, with central support of up to 60% and a target to reduce aggregate technical and commercial (AT & C) losses to 12-15%.The Union Budget 2026-27 allocates ₹18,000 crore to the scheme and ₹22,000 crore to PM Surya Ghar. India's target of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030 is expected to support continued investment in power distribution infrastructure.The company is also exploring opportunities in battery energy storage systems and transmission projects, which are additional to its existing revenue targets. Management has outlined revenue guidance of ₹1,000 crore for FY 2027-28.Management CommentaryMr. Santosh Shah, Managing Director and Promoter of Sugs Lloyd Limited, said:"H1 FY27 is the strongest half-year in our history. Revenue of ₹213.31 crore is up 73% and profit after tax of ₹20.01 crore is up 69%. On our last call we said that billing which slipped from June would come through in the second quarter, and it did: Q2 revenue of ₹134.91 crore is more than double the same quarter last year.We won seven orders worth ₹395 crore excluding GST in the quarter, led by an RDSS award for Punjab State Power Corporation in Faridkot and Gurdashpur Circle, which takes our distribution-reform work beyond Bihar, and three-year network O & M mandates from Tata Power's Odisha discoms. As of 30 September, our total order book stood at ₹1,068 crore, comprising ₹929 crore in Power T & D and ₹139 crore in Solar. In the Projects business, we continue to explore opportunities in transmission, SCADA and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to support our future growth.In parallel, development work is progressing in our Products business, with supplies of compact FPIs expected to commence in Q3 FY27. Development activities for VCBs and Ring Main Units (RMUs) are also underway as part of our product portfolio expansion. We are also evaluating strategies to increase the contribution of the Products business to our overall revenue.Our business remains weighted to the March quarter. Our focus for the rest of the year is execution discipline, collections and converting our qualified pipeline. The Board and management remain committed to building this business with discipline and to creating durable, long-term value for all our stakeholders."About Sugs Lloyd LimitedSugs Lloyd Limited is an EPC company engaged in Power T & D, solar and smart-grid solutions across India. Established in 2009 and listed on the BSE SME platform in September 2025, the company has developed capabilities in power infrastructure projects under national schemes such as RDSS and IPDS.Its operations combine transmission and distribution infrastructure, solar EPC execution, loss-reduction hardware, particularly fault passage indicators, and grid-automation systems.The company serves clients including NTPC, the Tata Power group, Adani Renewables, Indian Railways, Konkan Railways, NBPDCL, SBPDCL, PSPCL, NHAI and NPCL, along with several state distribution companies. It holds around 50% market share in Fault Passage Indicator technology.With more than 1,000 employees, Sugs Lloyd Limited has completed over 80 projects, solarised more than 5,000 government buildings and commissioned over 50,000 solar street lights. The company operates across 10 states and holds ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 27001 and ISO 45001 certifications.Investor RelationsNimmy Singh ChauhanCompany Secretary & Compliance OfficerEmail: compliance@sugslloyds.com Phone: +91-0120-4558247Address: 2nd Floor, Logix Park, Plot No. A4 & 5, Sector 16, Gautam Buddha Nagar, Noida, Uttar Pradesh 201301Website:www.sugslloyds.com DisclaimerThis document contains forward-looking statements, which are not historical facts and are subject to risks and uncertainties, including government actions, local developments, execution risk, order-book conversion, receivable cycles and technological change. headline: Brooks Local President Heather Fournier honoured with UNA Bread & Roses Award
content: Heather Fournier, president of Local 191 at the Brooks Health Centre, was honoured with the 2026 UNA Bread and Roses Award at the AGM on October 28. “For more than 14 years, Heather has demonstrated an unwavering commitment to the United Nurses of Alberta and to the members she represents,” wrote the UNA Local 191 members who nominated Fournier for the award. “During the past two years as local vice-president, she has consistently exemplified servant leadership through active participation at the local, employer and provincial levels, ensuring the voices of frontline health care workers are heard and respected.” A Registered Nurse at the hospital in Brooks, Fournier served as Local 191 vice-president before stepping into the role of president in 2026. She has served on both the professional responsibility and occupational health and safety committees, where she is known for working collaboratively with colleagues and the employer to improve working conditions, promote staff safety and advocate for high-quality patient care. “One of her most significant accomplishments has been her evidence-based advocacy for improved staffing,” wrote Fournier’s nominators. “Recognizing the impact staffing shortages were having on both patients and staff, she independently collected and analyzed unit data, carefully documenting trends and presenting well-supported recommendations through the appropriate union and organizational processes.” “Throughout every initiative, she has demonstrated professionalism, integrity, and respect for the collaborative process,” they wrote. “Her sustained involvement reflects not only her dedication to the Union, but also her unwavering commitment to improving healthcare for the members she represents and the patients they serve.” One of Fournier’s greatest strengths is the example she sets for those around her by being well prepared and taking the initiative to review policies, procedures and best practices to provide safe, knowledgeable care, her nominators wrote. “Her professionalism, strong communication skills, and willingness to support colleagues make her an approachable and trusted resource for both new and experienced members.”

headline: Dubai takes a shine to Kullu’s Sinduri pomegranates
content: New Delhi Noida-based Amama Exports shipped 1.3 tonnes after directly sourcing from four farmers of a village in the state’s Kullu district. While farmers have received 50 per cent higher rates than the local mandi by selling directly to an exporter, the firm has also received 40 per cent higher rate than its previous order from another destination. “Though we have been exporting pomegranate from other states, first time we sent the fruit from Kullu and the entire quantity was sold in a day in the supermarket in Dubai, which had placed the order. The importer was also impressed with the quality as such pomegranate was never bought by him,” said Tanmay Talwar, CEO of Amama Exports, which is into export of fruits and vegetables from India. Talwar also said that after sorting the pomegranate at farm level in Bhuntar in Kullu district, further sorting was done at the company’s Noida warehouse before it was packed and sent via air cargo from Delhi. Vir Singh Guleria, one of the four farmers who sold their pomegranate, told businessline: “I was in touch with APEDA’s Harpreet Singh to facilitate sales for export purpose. Finally, he got us in touch with Talwar and his team who came to our village to inspect the pomegranate at the garden itself.” He also said that the company paid at rate of Rs 210/kg whereas at that time pomegranate in local mandi was sold at Rs 130-140/kg. Singh, an assistant general manager with APEDA, said that the agency facilitated the export of Sinduri variety pomegranates from Kullu to Dubai on October 21. Hopefully more quantity of Himachal’s pomegranate will be shipped in the coming days, he added. According to the Horticulture Department of Himachal Pradesh, the state recorded pomegranate production of 1,638.05 tonnes across 347.50 hectares during FY 2025–26. India’s export of agri products, promoted by APEDA, to UAE was 3.81 million tonnes worth $ 2.6 billion in FY26. UAE is a leading destination of India’s $ 100 million worth annual pomegranate exports. the The UAE market could provide big opportunities for Himachal Pradesh’s horticultural produce if growers are linked with exporters under such initiatives, said an expert. “The export of these pomegranates reflects APEDA’s continued efforts to connect Indian farmers and Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) with international markets. Such initiatives create opportunities for better price realisation. By strengthening linkages between growers and exporters, we aim to expand market access for India’s diverse horticultural produce, enhance farmers’ incomes and enable more regional products to reach global consumers,” Abhishek Dev, Chairman of APEDA, said in a statement. APEDA has also identified persimmons, stone fruits, juices and ready-to-eat products from Himachal Pradesh which have potential in overseas markets. “Continued focus on quality management, market linkages and export compliance can help expand opportunities for local growers and strengthen the state’s participation in international agricultural trade,” Singh said. Talwar of Amama Export said that his firm will work with APEDA-recognised FPOs across states, so that growers in remote districts can reach buyers in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman and Europe.

headline: Rahul Gandhi must explain what Congress actually did to secure justice for 1984 Sikh genocide: Tarun Chugh
content: Chandigarh: Ahead of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's visit to Punjab, BJP leader Tarun Chugh on Tuesday asked him to answer questions surrounding the suffering of families affected by the "1984 Sikh genocide".."Punjab is not a state that can be influenced merely through political speeches and electoral visits. The people of Punjab have not forgotten the dark chapter of 1984, when innocent Sikhs were targeted and thousands of families had their lives changed forever," the Rajya Sabha MP said in a statement..Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge will participate in the 'Insaaf Rally' scheduled to be held in Punjab's Sangrur on Wednesday..Chugh said that the violence against Sikhs in 1984 was not merely a riot but one of the most painful chapters in India's history.."Families lost their loved ones, women lost their husbands and children, and countless children lost their parents. For these families, justice remains an unfinished struggle. Gandhi and the Congress leadership cannot continue to turn away from their questions..Rahul Gandhi turns up heat on PM Modi, says Bhagwat can judge their open debate."They must explain what the Congress party actually did to secure justice for the victims," he said..Gandhi and the Congress leadership choosing November 1 to organise a protest at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan was like rubbing salt into the wounds of families affected by the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.."A date associated with the horrific memories of thousands of innocent Sikhs being killed and families being destroyed should have demanded sensitivity and remembrance, not a political protest and show of strength," he said..Chugh also questioned the Punjab Congress leadership, saying that before welcoming Gandhi, party leaders Pargat Singh, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, Partap Singh Bajwa and every other Congress leader in Punjab must clearly state their position on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.."They must clarify whether they stand with the victim families and whether they have the courage to demand accountability for the Congress party's historical record, during which thousands of innocent Sikhs lost their lives and countless families were devastated. Punjab Congress leaders must move beyond political courtesies and rhetoric and demonstrate a clear commitment towards securing justice for the victims," he said.."Will he meet the families of the 1984 victims during his Punjab visit? Will he sit with them, listen to their suffering and respond to their long-pending questions?."Will he acknowledge the historical responsibility of the Congress party and make a clear commitment towards securing justice for the victims? Punjab does not need political rhetoric; it deserves sensitivity, accountability and justice," he said.

headline: APEDA expands export basket as Kullu ships 1.3 MT Sinduri pomegranates to Dubai
content: New Delhi [India], November 3 (ANI): In a move to expand the overseas footprint of regional horticulture beyond traditional fruit produce, the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the export of 1.3 metric tonnes (MT) of Sinduri variety pomegranates from the Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh to Dubai in the United Arab Emirates.The Ministry of Commerce & Industry stated that the outbound shipment comprised 650 boxes of two kilograms each and was handled by Uttar Pradesh-based Amama Exports. The procurement mechanism linked local cultivators and a Farmer Producer Organisation directly with the trading firm, creating an international trade pathway for the northern state's agrarian sector.The produce was procured from local orchards and the Bhuntar Farmer Producer Organisation, an entity representing around 600 agricultural growers. The Kullu district horticulture administration assisted the trade process through procurement support and ground-level coordination.The ministry noted that the commercial engagement delivered tangible income growth for the participating growers."The export enabled participating farmers to achieve 50% higher price realisation compared with the prevailing domestic market benchmark," the ministry stated. The ministry added that such linkages provide "additional marketing opportunities for growers, encourage quality-focused production and support greater participation of FPOs in agricultural exports."The Sinduri pomegranate is cultivated in Himachal Pradesh alongside the Bhagwa and Kandhari varieties. Characterised by red skin, juicy arils, and a balanced sweet-tart profile, the fruit meets parameters required for table consumption and long-distance cargo movement.APEDA Chairman Abhishek Dev officially flagged off the consignment during an event attended by trade authority officials, representatives of the state horticulture department, corporate exporters, farmer collectives, and local growers. The official engagement underscored institutional coordination between primary producers, trading houses, and regulatory authorities to establish reliable trade channels for regional horticulture.The bilateral trade route to West Asia remains a primary destination for Indian farm output. During the financial year 2025-26, India registered shipments of APEDA-scheduled agricultural and processed food products worth around USD 2.59 billion to the UAE, accounting for an aggregate volume of approximately 3.81 million metric tonnes.The dispatch of Kullu pomegranates forms part of a broader policy push to diversify Himachal Pradesh’s export base beyond its established apple trade. The state possesses commercial capacity to export other regional commodities, including persimmons, stone fruits, juices, and ready-to-eat items.The ministry observed that sustained attention to quality management, market connections, and export compliance will remain essential to widen avenues for regional growers and raise Himachal Pradesh's share in cross-border agricultural commerce. (ANI)

headline: Himachal to Recruit 2,423 Teachers for CBSE-Affiliated Government Schools; Applications from November 10
content: Hamirpur: The Himachal Pradesh Rajya Chayan Aayog, has issued an advertisement for the recruitment of 2,423 teachers in government schools affiliated with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE). The recruitment will cover 15 different subjects and will be carried out under a scheme-based contractual arrangement within the state’s Education Department. According to the advertisement, selected candidates will receive a fixed monthly honorarium of ₹30,000. The online application process will begin at 10:00 AM on November 10, while the last date for submitting applications is December 5, up to 11:59 PM. Mathematics has the highest number of vacancies, with 281 posts. English, Hindi, Biology, Sanskrit, Commerce and Physical Education have 187 vacancies each. Similarly, 156 posts each have been advertised for Political Science, History and Economics. For Physics, Chemistry, Computer Science and Music, 95 vacancies are available in each subject, while Fine Arts has 172 posts. Vikram Mahajan, Secretary of the State Selection Commission, said that eligible candidates would be able to submit their applications through the Commission’s official website from November 10 to December 5. The advertisement also provides details regarding the required educational qualifications, eligibility conditions, examination fees and selection procedure. Candidates have been advised to carefully go through the recruitment notification and eligibility requirements before submitting their applications.
